subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should this issue be resolved by a narrow `doctor.memory.status` provider fallback, or folded into the broader contract that status should not locally materialize memory plugins?
rationale: The remaining behavior crosses CLI status, gateway diagnostics, and plugin-runtime ownership, and current main plus the stale closing PR leave two plausible but conflicting fix shapes.

options.title: Fold into broader issue
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 as the canonical owner, close or replace the stale fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Revive surgical fallback
options.body: Ask for a refreshed PR that proves `status --deep` and JSON status trust live gateway provider evidence without changing plugin loader/runtime behavior.

options.title: Accept current wording
options.body: Declare `not checked` sufficient for skipped status inspection, document that memory health lives in `status --all` or memory-specific diagnostics, and close the linked PR path.

recommendation.title: Fold into broader issue
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 as the canonical owner, close or replace the stale fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the current status/runtime boundary is the memory-runtime plugin routing work and current-line ownership.
